clue.text: Generosity shown by head of state, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the letters come from how a phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: the head of the word State is its capital, a large S

explanation.surface: A monarch or president is reported to be lavish with gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of State is its initial, written as a capital or large S; saying 'large S' gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, which is generosity.

clue.text: Exercise needing fewer clothes?

parts.note: fewer means less
to have clothes on is to be wearing them, so ON stands for being clothed

explanation.surface: A workout that calls for stripping down to lighter kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing fewer clothes is having 'less on', which run together gives a classroom exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a piece of teaching or a set exercise for pupils.

clue.text: Heaps will fail them

parts.note: heaps here are old bangers, battered cars, which would not pass trials of driving on the highway

explanation.surface: Piles of something are doomed to flunk certain examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heaps' reads as piles, but it is slang for decrepit old cars, which fail driving trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests of a vehicle on public highways are what a dilapidated car would not pass.

clue.text: Being impatient, agree to differ

indicators.note: to differ asks the letters of the neighbouring word to take a different order

explanation.surface: Unwilling to wait, someone agrees to disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen and impatient for something to happen is eager for it.

clue.text: Ordeals suffered for the Admiral

indicators.note: ordeals that are suffered are knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval commander has endured hardships.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sea Lord is one of the senior admirals on the British Admiralty Board.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea Lords were the naval members of the Admiralty Board, admirals by rank.

clue.text: Not quite accurate summary

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a letter short of complete, losing its final one

parts.note: accurate means precise

explanation.surface: An abstract that is a little off the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a short abstract of a longer text.

clue.text: Old master takes class in new term

indicators.note: in places the class word inside the rearranged letters of term
new signals that the letters of term are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a brand is a class or kind of goods

explanation.surface: A great painter signs up for lessons as a new academic term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is only a link; 'in' is the container signal and 'new' the anagram signal, so the painter's name wraps around the class word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt is the Dutch painter of the seventeenth century, a classic Old Master.

clue.text: Queen's favourite company gets right type of soldier

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A monarch's best-loved firm hires a certain kind of military man.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth II was famous for keeping Welsh corgis.
explanation.definitionFit: The late Queen Elizabeth II kept dozens of these short-legged Welsh dogs as pets.

clue.text: Old poet endlessly follows us around, causing anxiety

indicators.note: follows puts the poet piece after the turned-round us
around turns the little word us the other way round
endlessly takes the final letter off the poet's name

parts.note: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A classic writer trails after us, making us nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the reversal signal and 'endlessly' clips the last letter; Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, is a standard crossword old poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of anxious uncertainty; 'causing anxiety' stands for the noun loosely as what creates such tension.

clue.text: How to impress someone in China?

definitions.meaning: impress here means press-gang, forcing someone into service as a sailor
a great port city found in China

explanation.surface: Seeking tips for making a good impression on a Chinese contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impress' looks like dazzle but means conscript by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai a man is to kidnap him into a ship's crew, and the city lies in China.

clue.text: Clever bit of song writing it's what Sting does

parts.note: smart means clever

indicators.note: bit of takes just the opening letter of song

explanation.surface: A rock star's clever songwriting, the craft he practises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' reads as the singer, but a sting is a wound that smarts; 'writing it's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting hurts sharply, and to hurt with a sharp pain is to smart.

clue.text: Witch doctor without article is a fake

indicators.note: without means the article is removed from the witch doctor

parts.note: a shaman is a tribal healer or witch doctor
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A medicine man with no credentials turns out to be a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a counterfeit or pretence, something not genuine.

clue.text: Animal more excited if given head's start

indicators.note: the animal would become the more-excited word if given the extra letter, so that letter is absent here

parts.note: hotter means more excited or heated

indicators.note: start means the first letter of head

explanation.surface: A creature grows more agitated when someone gets a head start.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus H (head's start) makes HOTTER, so the answer is HOTTER without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a fish-eating river mammal.

clue.text: White rose cultivated in a different way

indicators.note: cultivated plays on gardening, signalling the letters of the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden white rose grown by an unusual method.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means differently, in another manner.

clue.text: Take off a broadcast about conservative

indicators.note: about means the broadcast word goes round the conservative letter

parts.note: to broadcast a signal is to send it out

explanation.surface: Removing a programme that discusses a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' reads as remove, but it means rise into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft taking off rises, climbing upward.

clue.text: Drained, like many were in wartime

definitions.meaning: emptied out, as a bowel or vessel is
city children were moved out to the country for safety during the war

explanation.definitionFit: Emptied of contents, and removed from danger as wartime children were from British cities.

clue.text: Periods when dynamos break down

indicators.note: machines that break down fall apart, so the letters of dynamos are rearranged

explanation.surface: Times when the generators fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests machinery failing; the days of the week often dreaded are what the shuffled letters give.
explanation.definitionFit: The first weekday recurs each week, a regular period of time.

clue.text: Sort of rabbit with some stuffing, gives that special flavour

indicators.note: with some stuffing means the rabbit word is filled with the extra letters

parts.note: the angora is a breed of rabbit with long fine fur

indicators.note: some takes only part of the word stuffing, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A breed of rabbit, cooked with stuffing, gains a distinctive taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the opening of 'stuffing' and 'with' has it filling the rabbit breed; angostura is the aromatic bitters used in cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura bitters are a flavouring used in drinks such as pink gin.

clue.text: What loaded gun had, as indicated in report

parts.note: a loaded gun has a bullet in it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An account says what was inside the loaded firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: A loaded gun has a 'bullet in'; 'as indicated' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news report.

clue.text: Social climber possibly puts skill last

indicators.note: last places the skill word at the end
possibly suggests puts may be arranged some other way

parts.note: art means skill

explanation.surface: An ambitious person might put craft at the bottom of the list.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves arrogantly, a social climber.

clue.text: Current leads to this in Dublin, eventually

indicators.note: leads to means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A trend that will reach the Irish capital in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide is the regular current of the sea.

clue.text: Mark time in one's declining years

parts.note: a dot is a small mark
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Noting the passing of time in later life.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the feeble state of old age.

clue.text: Time to worry — what working mothers want!

parts.note: a day is a period of time
to care is to be troubled or concerned

explanation.surface: Time for anxiety, as parents with jobs know.
explanation.definitionFit: Childminding provided during the working day lets parents go out to their jobs.

clue.text: Minor insult

explanation.definitionFit: Slight means trivial as an adjective, and as a noun a snub.

clue.text: Period of confinement in the US?

definitions.text: Period of confinement in the US?

parts.words: Period of confinement in the US?
parts.note: confinement is childbirth, and a day spent giving birth would be named after the work of delivery, also an American public holiday

explanation.surface: A spell of imprisonment in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confinement' suggests prison but is old-fashioned for childbirth; the American holiday in September has the name of a day in childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: The US workers' holiday in September shares its name with a day spent in childbirth.

clue.text: Obscure blood group is printed on the cover

parts.note: to blur is to obscure
B is one of the blood groups

explanation.surface: A hard-to-read blood type label on a medical folder.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the promotional text printed on a book's jacket.

clue.text: Only solution that contains disinfectant

indicators.note: that contains means the answer lies inside the words before it

explanation.surface: The single liquid with a germ-killer in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysol is a brand of disinfectant cleaner.

clue.text: Holds up free transport

definitions.meaning: rides given for nothing in someone's car

explanation.definitionFit: To lift is to raise, and a lift is a free ride in someone's vehicle.

clue.text: Time with relations in digs

parts.note: aunts are relations

explanation.surface: A spell staying with family in lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like British slang for lodgings, but it means jibes.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs are pointed remarks, jeers.

clue.text: A long way off, like best discus throw

definitions.meaning: the winning discus has been hurled the greatest distance

explanation.definitionFit: Remote and distant, and literally hurled a great distance.

clue.text: Not anyone could produce a cipher

explanation.definitionFit: No person at all, and an insignificant person, a cipher.

clue.text: Actors follow important points in making 18

indicators.note: follow puts the actors after the compass points

parts.note: the cardinal points of the compass are N, E, W and S
the cast is the actors in a play

explanation.surface: Players come after key moments in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' refers to the answer of 18 down, BULLETIN; 'in making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast news report is a bulletin.
